Selected path: the Class D Operator’s License includes passenger cars [A03].
The knowledge tests assess sign recognition and the state’s road rules, vehicle laws and safe-driving practices [A04].
Selected topic: graduated licensing and first-time adult applicants; instructional emphasis is authored coverage policy rather than a verified percentage of the exam.

Audience: first-time Delaware passenger-car applicants studying graduated licensing and first-time adult applicants. Instruction stays within the selected Class D path; specialty-license material on mixed pages is outside this dossier.
The Level One eligibility rule covers applicants from age sixteen until eighteen and the active-IEP pathway until twenty-two [A01].
First-time adult applicants receive a learner permit after passing vision screening and knowledge exams [A02].
Learning level: explain each cited definition or rule in plain language before using it in a practice scenario. Section grouping and emphasis are authored teaching choices; no official topic weights are asserted.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
The graduated-license program gives eligible new drivers more supervised experience while limiting exposure to high-risk situations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
A signatory parent or sponsor participates in the graduated-license applicant’s training and decides when more driving authority is appropriate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
A person aged 18 or older may opt out of the graduated-license program, requiring no sponsor but requiring DMV vision, knowledge and road-skills exams. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A02
The Level One graduated learner permit is available from age 16 until age 18, or from age 16 until age 22 for a person on an active Individualized Education Program. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A02
A Level One applicant using a Delaware driver education course must present its Blue or White Driver Education Certificate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A02
An out-of-state driver education certificate must receive Delaware Department of Education approval, and the applicant must present that approval to DMV. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A02
A regular-license GDL applicant must document identity, lawful presence and a Social Security number when eligible, and normally supply two Delaware residence proofs unless the same-address Delaware-licensed-sponsor waiver applies. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A02
The two residence proofs are waived when the sponsor holds a Delaware license and shares the applicant’s address. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
Every graduated-license application requires a sponsor’s signature. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
The sponsor and graduated-license applicant share liability for damages caused by the applicant’s negligence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
The sponsor decides whether the graduated-license applicant can responsibly operate a vehicle and chooses who may supervise driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
A stepparent may sponsor a graduated-license applicant only after adopting the applicant or becoming the applicant’s legal guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
Parents listed as sponsors are verified using an original or certified birth certificate naming the relevant parent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A03
A legal guardian or court-appointed custodian appointed under Delaware law may act as the applicant’s sponsor. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A03
A suitable person approved by the Secretary of Transportation or Chief of Driver Services may act as the applicant’s sponsor. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A03
The sponsor must sign the license application in front of a DMV licensing employee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A03
During the graduated-license program’s 12 months, the signing sponsor may withdraw endorsement and end the applicant’s driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A03
For a minor who has finished the graduated-license program, the sponsor may still withdraw endorsement until the driver turns 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
A graduated-license applicant must pay the $50 fee for an eight-year Class D license and pass vision screening at application. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
A driver education teacher identifies graduated-license applicants who need specialized evaluation, training or equipment because of disability for testing by the DMV. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
A Level One driver must carry the permit while driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
While a Level One driver’s vehicle is moving, the driver and passengers must use seat belts or appropriate child safety or booster seats. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
A Level One driver cannot operate a vehicle while using a mobile phone, texting device or similar electronic device. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
During the first 12 months of Level One driving authority, passengers are limited to an adult supervisor and one additional person, except that immediate family members may ride when the supervisor is present. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
During mandatory supervision, the supervisor must be a properly licensed parent, guardian or sponsor-approved driver aged at least 25 who has held a Class D license for at least five years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A03
During mandatory supervision, the supervising driver must occupy the front seat beside the permit holder while the vehicle moves. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A03
During mandatory supervision, nobody besides the supervising driver may share the front seat with the permit holder. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A03
A Level One driver must remain supervised throughout the first six months after permit issuance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A03
The sponsor must certify 50 hours of driving practice, including 10 hours at night, during the Level One driver’s initial supervised period. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A03
The supervised-driving certification is submitted to the Department of Education after the initial six months of valid driving authority. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

Misconceptions: A graduated-license supervisor and an adult learner’s accompanying driver follow different qualification rules.
Mnemonics: Use “permit, sponsor, supervisor” as an authored cue to separate the documents and people in the cited requirements.
Glossary: GDL means graduated driver licensing; the Level One permit is the restricted permit described in this section.
Dynamic facts: Agency contact information, submission email addresses and web links require current confirmation and are withheld from stable knowledge.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
A foreign-language name-change document used for a Driving Privilege Card requires a professional English translation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A01
Under the Driving Privilege Card table, photocopies, bill printouts and nonbusiness letters or cards cannot serve as residence proofs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A01
Driving Privilege Card residence-proof mail must arrive through USPS and be postmarked or received within 60 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A01
The two Driving Privilege Card residence proofs must come from separate sources and show a physical address rather than a post-office box. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A02
When both parents live together in Delaware and the minor lives with them, either parent is the preferred graduated-license sponsor. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A02
When a minor lives only with one parent in Delaware, that resident parent may sponsor the application. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A02
When the applicant lives with neither parent and has no Delaware legal guardian, a parent living in Delaware may sponsor the application. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A04
After the initial six months of valid Level One driving authority, unsupervised driving is permitted from 6 a.m. until 10 p.m. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A04
After six months of valid Level One driving authority, driving from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. requires supervision unless travel is directly to or from church, work, or the permit holder’s school activities on school property. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A04
During the second six-month period, a Level One driver traveling without a supervisor may carry only one other passenger. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A04
During the second six-month period, the immediate-family passenger exception applies only when an adult supervisor is present. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A04
Violating Level One permit restrictions is treated as driving without a license and results in a two-month suspension for a first offense. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A04
A subsequent violation of Level One permit restrictions results in a four-month suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A04
A Level One driver younger than 18 may receive a Class D license after completing the 12-month program if the sponsor’s endorsement remains valid and driving privileges are not suspended, revoked, canceled, denied or surrendered. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A04
A Level One holder aged 18 or older may qualify for a Class D license by completing the 12-month GDL requirements with sponsor endorsement and no suspension, revocation, cancellation, denial or surrender, or by taking DMV vision, written and road-skills exams. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A04
A Level One permit automatically converts to a Class D license after a full 12 months of valid driving authority. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A04
Time during suspension, revocation, cancellation, denial or surrender does not count toward the Level One driver’s required 12 months. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R18 | anchor: A04
A Level One driver whose privileges were suspended, revoked, canceled, denied or surrendered must add an equivalent period of valid driving experience and undergo complete testing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R19 | anchor: A04
A first-time adult learner permit is issued after the applicant passes vision screening and the knowledge exams. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R20 | anchor: A04
A first-time adult applicant owes payment at application and must pass all examinations within 12 months. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R21 | anchor: A04
An adult learner must drive with a licensed person aged at least 21 who is qualified for the vehicle class being practiced. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R22 | anchor: A04
A first-time adult applicant cannot take the road examination until at least 30 days after passing the knowledge exam. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R23 | anchor: A02
The graduated-license sponsor options are listed in preference order, beginning with the eligible parent arrangements described by the handbook. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R24 | anchor: A03
The remaining sponsor preference list ranks a Delaware-appointed legal guardian or court-appointed custodian ahead of another suitable person approved by the Secretary of Transportation or Chief of Driver Services. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]
